2. The facts, relevant for disposal of the appeal, are that the present respondents instituted Title Suit No. 42 of 2003 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Kotalipara, Gopalgonj, impleading the defendants-appellant herein and others praying for a declaration that the judgment and decree dated 27-5-2003 obtained by the defendant in Title Suit No. 06 of 2003 (decree signed on 1-6-2003) is collusive, illegal and not binding upon the plaintiffs. In the plaint it is contended that while Annada Charan Saha, Kanjiram Saha, Jotnamoyee Saha, Narayan Chandra Sana, Rakhal Chandra Saha, Hare Krishna Saha, Mohendra Kumar Saha and Amullay Kumar Saha along with their other co-sharers were possessing the suit land as being lawful owners RS Khatian Nos. 155, 27 and 40 and SA Khatian Nos. 134, 27 and 40 were correctly prepared in their names. Mohendra Kumar Saha died leaving behind his son Ranjan Kumar Saha who became the owner of 1.27 acre of land appertaining to Mouza-Unsia, who transferred the entire 1.27 acre of land in SA khatian No. 27, plot No. 451 and 452, SA Khatian No. 134, Plot Nos. 84 and 85 and in khatian No. 40 Plot No. 451 of No. 66 Amtoli Mouza to one Jogesh Chandra Dhupi vide deed No. 4595 dated 3-5-0975 and deed No.5193 dated 6-6-1975. Jogesh Chandra Dhupi thereafter transferred the said 1.27 acre of land to the plaintiff-respondent No. 1 vide deed No. 3449 dated 16-8-1982 and since then the plaintiff has been enjoying the same upon constructing house and planting trees. Other co-sharers Annada Charan Saha, Kanjiram Saha, Jotnamoyee Saha, Narayan Chandra' Saha and Hare Krishan Saha also sold out 0.94 acre of land from the aforesaid plots as described in the schedule to the plaint to the plaintiff-respondents-Abul Kashem Bepari, the father of defendant Nos. 1-7 and husband of the defendant No. 8 vide deed No. 4992 dated 7-7-1985 pursuant to which the plaintiff got 0.63 acre of land in 2/3 rd share and the said Abul Kashem Bepari died leaving behind defendants No. 1-8 who inherited the said 0.31 acre of land. The plaintiff-respondent No. 1 sold out 0.25 1/3 acre of land out of 0.31 acre, which he got vide deed No. 4992 dated 7-7-1985 to the defendant No. 8 (mother of defendant Nos. 1-7) vide deed No. 1325 dated 19-9-1990 and, as such, defendant Nos. 1-8 became owners of 0.31+25 1/3 = 0.56 1/3 acre of land and the plaintiffs-respondents became owners of 1.64½ decimal of land. Under these circumstances defendant Nos. 1-8 filed Title Suit No. 6 of 2003 for declaration of title and confirmation of possession over 0.72½ acre of land, as described in the schedule `Kha' to the plaint. In the said suit, Harihar Biswas, the defendant-petitioner No. 9 was made defendant No. 1 and Chandra Kanta Saha and Lalit Mohan Saha two dead persons were made defendants Nos. 2 and 3 respectively without impleading the present plaintiff-respondent as party in the suit who are in possession of the suit land being its lawful owners and thereby obtained a collusive sole decree (compromise decree) on 27-5-2003. When on the basis of such collusive decree they threatened the plaintiff respondents on 2-6-2003 to evict them from the suit land, then the plaintiff came to know about the said collusive and illegal decree which is not binding upon the plaintiffs. Hence, they filed the suit. 

 3. Defendants Nos. 1, 3, 7 and 8 contested the suit by filing written statement, contending, inter alia, that the suit is barred by limitation and for mis-joinder and non joinder of parties. The suit land, appertaining to Mouza Amtali, RS Khatian No. 40 measuring 1.01 acre was owned and possessed admittedly by Annada Chandra Saha and his co-sharers in their respective shares within the same Mouza, another 1.01acre land appertaining to RS Khatian No. 27 was also owned and possessed by the above noted persons in their respective shares. The said Sahas owned and possessed 0.44 acre of land in Unisa Mouza appertaining to RS Khatian No. 155 in their respective shares. On 15 Poush, 1357 BS Chandra Kanto Saha and Lalit Mohon Saha gave 0.72½ acre of land in favour of Abul Kashem Bepari, the father of defendant Nos. 1-7 as Rayati settlement on which the said Abul Kashem erected his house, planted trees and was living peacefully before he died leaving behind defendant Nos. 1-7 as his sons and daughters and defendant No. 8, his wife as heirs. As one Harihar BiswaS and others threatened them to disposes from the said land the defendant Nos. 1-8 filed Title Suit No. 6 of 2003 against the said Harihar Biswas, Chandra Kanto and Lalit Mohan Saha as defendants wherein summons were issued upon them. Since Chandra Kanto Saha and Lalit Mohan Saha had no interest in the suit land they did not appear before the court in the said suit but Harihar Biswas appeared and upon admitting the right, title and interest of defendant Nos. 1-8 over the suit land executed a solenama in their favour, on the basis of which the suit was decreed in terms of the solenama. Hence, the present defendants were owning and possessing the said 0.72½ acre of land for over 12 years. Late Abul Kashem Bepari purchased 0.25 acre of land from one Usha Rani, vide deed No. 964 dated 16-9-1972 and defendant No. 8 Ayesha Bibi purchased 0.25 acre of land from plaintiff No. 1 vide deed No. 2324 dated 19-9-1990. Chandra Kanto Saha and Lalit Mohon Saha sold 0.95 acre of land to the plaintiffs and late Abul Kashem Bepari from RS Khatian Nos. 27, 40 and 155 out of which the share of Abul Kashem Bepari has been inherited by defendant Nos. 1-8 and, as such, the defendants are owning and possessing 1.54¼ acre of land for a period of 12 years. The plaintiffs Irive no possession in the suit land and they have filed the suit with false and concocted story of purchase on the basis of a forged deed dated 16-8-1982. Hence, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 7. Mr M Quamrul Haque Siddique, the learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the appellants submits that the High Court Division has erred in law in reversing the judgment and decree, passed by the appellate Court without adverting to the findings of the appellate Court that Chandra Kanta Saha and Lolit Mohon Saha had in total 0.72½ acre of land in their share of RS Khatian Nos. 27, 40 and 155, which were acquired by Abul Kashem Bepari by pattan. 

 12. Upon perusal of the plaint, it transpires that the plaintiffs filed the suit only for declaration that the sole decree (compromise decree) dated 27-5-2003 and decree signed on 1-6-2003 is collusive, null and void and not binding upon the plaintiffs. The said sole decree was passed in respect of 72½ decimals land described in schedule `Kha' to the plaint. The plaintiffs claim title in respect of 2.21 acres land described in schedule 'Ka' which appertaining in different khatians and 4 (four) plots.
